note:
240 candidate hard queries (40 per category) for the taxonomy v3 tier, per PLAN-2026-08-13 E4 and the decisions recorded in docs/17.

This file is NOT a query set that runs. It is the pool the pilot draws from: all 240 are scored against two vendors, and the 150 that score lowest (25 per category) are promoted into full-v1.json as tier 2. Difficulty is therefore a measured filter rather than an authoring claim, which matters because docs/16 established that the saturation is caused by the queries and nothing else - so a hard tier that turns out not to be hard would waste the whole exercise.

Same six categories and the same field shape as full-v1.json, deliberately: E4 calls for an added tier in the existing format, not a parallel benchmark.

Decay rule (full-v1.json explains it): breaking_news carries no gold_answer and is phrased perpetually, because a freshness query with a fixed answer becomes a general-knowledge query within weeks. The same trap is sharper in this tier than in the standard one - a hard code_technical query is tempting to write against 'the latest version', which decays the same way, so those are pinned to a named version instead. local_shopping and long_tail carry no gold_answer for the same reason the standard tier does not: prices and research consensus both move.

Where a gold answer was not certain enough to assert, it is omitted rather than guessed. A wrong gold_answer is worse than none: the rubric shows it to the judge as 'Known correct answer', so an error there does not add noise, it inverts the grade. The pilot flags any query where all vendors agree on something the gold contradicts.

Difficulty levers, by category: breaking_news asks for a current value AND a second fact rather than an entity name; general_facts moves to obscure-but-documented, multi-part answers; multi_hop goes to three hops; code_technical targets version-pinned migration and deprecation detail in less-popular libraries; local_shopping stacks three or more simultaneous constraints; long_tail narrows to questions with thin web coverage.

False-premise questions are deliberately absent, and they are the strongest remaining lever. They need a rubric clause saying that confidently answering a false premise is a failure, and docs/16 measured that rubric edits shift the score level - so that change has to be made and measured on its own, not smuggled in with a query set.

queries.text: Where is the world's longest-running laboratory experiment housed, and what property does it measure?

queries.text: Which two cities were struck by atomic weapons in 1945, and on which dates?

queries.text: Which planet is the hottest in the Solar System, and why is it hotter than the planet closest to the Sun?

queries.text: The physicist who supervised Richard Feynman's doctoral thesis later worked on a theory of gravitation with a student who coined a famous term in astrophysics. What is that term?

queries.text: The company that first commercialised the transistor radio later became a major camera manufacturer. What was the company's original name when it was founded?

queries.text: The author of the novel that inspired the film Blade Runner also wrote a novel adapted into a film starring Keanu Reeves. What is the name of that film, and in what year was it released?
queries.gold_answer: Philip K. Dick; A Scanner Darkly, released in 2006

queries.text: The mathematician who introduced the concept of a Turing machine studied for his PhD under a logician at Princeton. Who was that supervisor, and what theorem is he best known for?

queries.text: The capital city of the country that hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics is not its largest city. What is the capital, and what is the population of the largest city?

queries.text: The programming language created by Guido van Rossum was named after a British comedy troupe. Which member of that troupe directed a 1985 dystopian film, and what was it called?

queries.text: The scientist who discovered penicillin shared a Nobel Prize with two others. One of them was born in Germany; which university did he flee to, and in what year did he leave Germany?

queries.text: The longest river in Asia flows through a dam that is the largest power station in the world by installed capacity. What is the dam called, and what is that capacity?
queries.gold_answer: The Yangtze; the Three Gorges Dam, with roughly 22,500 megawatts installed capacity

queries.text: The founder of the company that makes the Unreal Engine also created a shareware game in the 1990s. What was that game, and what genre was it?
queries.gold_answer: Tim Sweeney of Epic Games created ZZT, a puzzle/adventure game with an included editor

queries.text: The chemist who developed the process for fixing atmospheric nitrogen shared his name with a process co-developed by an industrialist. Who was the industrialist, and what is the combined process called?
queries.gold_answer: Fritz Haber and Carl Bosch; the Haber-Bosch process

queries.text: The country with the largest reserves of lithium by some estimates sits in a region known as a triangle with two neighbours. Name the three countries and the region.
queries.gold_answer: Bolivia, Chile and Argentina, in the Lithium Triangle

queries.text: The architect of the Sagrada Familia died in an accident. What kind of accident, in what year, and is the building finished?
queries.gold_answer: Antoni Gaudi was struck by a tram in 1926; the basilica remains unfinished

queries.text: The operating system that Linus Torvalds studied while writing Linux was created by a professor for teaching. Who was the professor, and what was the operating system called?

queries.text: The composer of the Goldberg Variations had a son who was also a noted composer and worked in London. Which son, and what was he known as?
queries.gold_answer: Johann Sebastian Bach's son Johann Christian Bach, known as the London Bach

queries.text: The battle that ended the Western Roman Empire's control of Italy is disputed, but the last emperor was deposed by a Germanic leader. Who was the emperor, who deposed him, and in what year?
queries.gold_answer: Romulus Augustulus was deposed by Odoacer in 476

queries.text: The inventor of the World Wide Web worked at a physics laboratory when he proposed it. What is the laboratory, in which two countries does its site sit, and in what year was the proposal written?
queries.gold_answer: CERN, straddling Switzerland and France; Tim Berners-Lee's proposal was written in 1989

queries.text: The author of The Left Hand of Darkness was the child of an anthropologist. Who was the parent, and what work is that parent best known for?
queries.gold_answer: Ursula K. Le Guin, daughter of Alfred Kroeber, known for his work with Ishi and California anthropology

queries.text: Two scientists who shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Henri Becquerel later had an element named jointly after them. What is the element, and what is its atomic number?
queries.gold_answer: Curium, named after Pierre and Marie Curie; atomic number 96

queries.text: The city that hosted the first modern Olympic Games is the capital of a country whose currency changed in 2001. What was the old currency, and what replaced it?
queries.gold_answer: Athens, Greece; the drachma was replaced by the euro

queries.text: The physicist who proposed the exclusion principle also lent his name to an effect involving equipment failure. What is the principle, and what is the informal effect called?
queries.gold_answer: Wolfgang Pauli; the Pauli exclusion principle and the informal 'Pauli effect'

queries.text: The database system that popularised the term NoSQL movement in 2009 was named at a meetup in San Francisco. Who organised it, and which database was the meetup originally about?
queries.gold_answer: Johan Oskarsson organised the 2009 meetup; the term was reused for a gathering about distributed non-relational databases including Cassandra and HBase

queries.text: The world's largest producer of copper shares a long border with the world's largest producer of lithium by reserves. Name both countries and the mountain range along their border.
queries.gold_answer: Chile produces the most copper and borders Bolivia and Argentina, both major lithium holders; the border range is the Andes

queries.text: The film that won the first Academy Award for Best Picture was silent. What was it called, and which film won the first Best Picture award for a talkie?
queries.gold_answer: Wings won the first Best Picture; The Broadway Melody was the first sound film to win

queries.text: The scientist who first isolated insulin shared a Nobel Prize and later shared his prize money. Who was he, who did he share the money with, and why?
queries.gold_answer: Frederick Banting shared his prize money with Charles Best, who had been omitted from the award

queries.text: The language with the most native speakers in South America is not Spanish. What is it, how many speakers roughly, and in which country?
queries.gold_answer: Portuguese, with over 200 million speakers, in Brazil

queries.text: The observatory that first detected gravitational waves has two widely separated sites. Where are they, and why does the detection require two?
queries.gold_answer: LIGO, at Hanford in Washington and Livingston in Louisiana; two sites allow coincidence detection to reject local noise and help localise the source

queries.text: The founder of the company behind the first mass-produced personal computer with a graphical interface later founded another computer company. Name the person, the second company, and what happened to it.
queries.gold_answer: Steve Jobs founded NeXT, which Apple acquired in 1996-97, bringing him back to Apple

queries.text: The treaty that established the European Economic Community was signed in a city that is also the capital of Italy. In what year was it signed, and how many countries signed it?
queries.gold_answer: The Treaty of Rome, signed in 1957 by six countries

queries.text: The astronomer who first measured the speed of light did so by observing a moon of Jupiter. Who was he, which moon, and roughly in what year?
queries.gold_answer: Ole Romer, observing Io, around 1676

queries.text: The cipher machine broken at Bletchley Park had a rotor design. What was the machine called, who designed the bombe used against it, and what was a key operational weakness exploited?
queries.gold_answer: Enigma; Alan Turing and Gordon Welchman designed the bombe; a key weakness was that no letter could encipher to itself, plus predictable cribs

queries.text: The largest moon in the Solar System orbits which planet, and is it larger than any planet?
queries.gold_answer: Ganymede orbits Jupiter and is larger than Mercury

queries.text: The economist who described creative destruction was born in a country that no longer exists. Who was he, what was the country, and what is the region called now?
queries.gold_answer: Joseph Schumpeter, born in Moravia in Austria-Hungary, now part of the Czech Republic

queries.text: The first vaccine ever developed targeted a disease later declared eradicated. Who developed it, against what disease, and in what year was eradication certified?
queries.gold_answer: Edward Jenner, against smallpox; eradication was certified in 1980

queries.text: The strait separating Asia from North America is named after an explorer. Who was he, what nationality, and whose navy did he sail for?
queries.gold_answer: Vitus Bering, a Dane who sailed for the Russian navy

queries.text: The compression algorithm behind the ZIP format was co-invented by two people. Name the algorithm, both inventors, and the year of the founding paper.
queries.gold_answer: The DEFLATE format builds on LZ77 by Abraham Lempel and Jacob Ziv, published in 1977

queries.text: The highest mountain on Earth sits on the border between two countries. Name both, give the mountain's name in each country's language, and say which side the standard commercial route ascends from.
queries.gold_answer: Nepal and China (Tibet); Sagarmatha in Nepali and Chomolungma in Tibetan; the most-used commercial route is the South Col route from Nepal

queries.text: The person who coined the term 'artificial intelligence' organised a 1956 workshop. Who was he, where was the workshop held, and who else is considered a founder of the field from it?
queries.gold_answer: John McCarthy; the Dartmouth workshop; other founders present included Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon and Nathaniel Rochester

queries.text: The novel that gave its name to a psychological catch-22 was set in which war, and what is the definition of the catch in the book?
queries.gold_answer: Catch-22 by Joseph Heller, set in the Second World War; a pilot asking to be grounded for insanity thereby demonstrates sanity

queries.text: The unit of frequency is named after a physicist who demonstrated electromagnetic waves. Who was he, in what decade did he do it, and whose theory did it confirm?
queries.gold_answer: Heinrich Hertz, in the 1880s, confirming Maxwell's theory

queries.text: The largest active volcano on Earth sits on an island chain formed by a hotspot. Name the volcano, the island, and explain what a hotspot is.
queries.gold_answer: Mauna Loa on Hawaii's Big Island; a hotspot is a persistent plume of rising mantle material that builds volcanoes as a plate moves over it

queries.text: In Python 3.12, what exactly changed about the behaviour of the `type` statement for generic aliases, and how does it differ from a plain assignment alias?
queries.gold_answer: PEP 695 added the `type X = ...` statement, creating a lazily evaluated TypeAliasType rather than eagerly binding a name

queries.text: In PostgreSQL, what is the difference between a MATERIALIZED and NOT MATERIALIZED CTE, and which version made the optimiser able to inline CTEs by default?
queries.gold_answer: PostgreSQL 12 began inlining non-recursive CTEs by default; MATERIALIZED forces the old behaviour of computing the CTE separately

queries.text: How do I make a Rust async function cancel-safe when used inside tokio::select!, and what is the specific hazard if it is not?
queries.gold_answer: A future dropped mid-poll loses partial state; cancel-safe futures must not buffer data that would be lost, and unsafe patterns should be wrapped in a task or use a cancel-safe API

queries.text: In React 18 and later, why does StrictMode invoke effects twice in development, and what class of bug is that designed to surface?
queries.gold_answer: It double-invokes mount effects to surface missing cleanup functions and non-idempotent setup, preparing for reusable state

queries.text: What is the difference between `COPY` and `ADD` in a Dockerfile, and in which specific cases is `ADD` still the correct choice?
queries.gold_answer: ADD additionally supports remote URLs and automatic extraction of local tar archives; COPY is preferred otherwise

queries.text: In Kubernetes, what is the difference between a readiness probe and a startup probe, and what failure does the startup probe specifically prevent?
queries.gold_answer: A startup probe disables the other probes until the app has started, preventing a slow-starting container from being killed by the liveness probe

queries.text: In SQLite, what does WAL mode change about concurrency, and what is the specific limitation on readers and writers?
queries.gold_answer: Write-ahead logging lets readers proceed concurrently with a writer, but still allows only one writer at a time, and the database must be on local disk

queries.text: How do I correctly implement `__hash__` alongside `__eq__` in Python, and what happens if I define only `__eq__`?
queries.gold_answer: Defining __eq__ sets __hash__ to None, making instances unhashable; you must define __hash__ explicitly and keep it consistent with equality

queries.text: In Go, what changed about loop variable scoping in version 1.22, and what bug did the previous behaviour cause?
queries.gold_answer: Go 1.22 gives each iteration its own loop variable; previously a single shared variable caused goroutines and closures to observe the final value

queries.text: What is the difference between `git rebase --onto` and a plain rebase, and give the exact form for moving a branch off the wrong base.
queries.gold_answer: git rebase --onto <newbase> <oldbase> <branch> replays only commits after oldbase onto newbase, unlike a plain rebase which uses the branch's merge base

queries.text: In TypeScript, what is the difference between `unknown` and `any`, and what narrowing is required before using an `unknown` value?
queries.gold_answer: unknown is assignable from anything but not assignable to anything without narrowing via a type guard, assertion or check; any disables checking entirely

queries.text: How does Postgres decide between a sequential scan and an index scan, and which specific planner setting is most often misconfigured on SSD-backed systems?
queries.gold_answer: The planner compares estimated costs; random_page_cost defaults to 4 and is usually too high on SSDs, discouraging index scans

queries.text: In Python asyncio, what is the difference between `asyncio.gather` and `asyncio.TaskGroup`, and what changed about exception handling?
queries.gold_answer: TaskGroup, added in 3.11, cancels remaining tasks on failure and raises an ExceptionGroup; gather with return_exceptions=False leaves siblings running

queries.text: What is the N+1 query problem in an ORM, and what are two distinct mechanisms for fixing it in SQLAlchemy?
queries.gold_answer: Lazy loading issues one query per parent row; fix with joinedload (a JOIN) or selectinload (a second IN query)

queries.text: In HTTP, what is the practical difference between a 502 and a 504 from a reverse proxy, and what does each tell you about where to look?
queries.gold_answer: 502 means the upstream returned an invalid response or refused the connection; 504 means the upstream did not respond within the proxy's timeout

queries.text: How do I pin transitive dependencies reproducibly with pip, and what does a hash-checking requirements file require of every entry?
queries.gold_answer: Use a lock file such as pip-compile output with --generate-hashes; hash-checking mode requires every dependency including transitive ones to be pinned with hashes

queries.text: In Rust, when do I need `Pin`, and what invariant does it enforce that `&mut T` does not?
queries.gold_answer: Pin guarantees the value will not be moved in memory, which self-referential futures require; &mut T permits moving out via mem::swap or replace

queries.text: What does `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` solve in a job queue, and what is the failure mode without SKIP LOCKED?
queries.gold_answer: It lets concurrent workers claim different rows; without it, workers block on the same locked rows and serialise

queries.text: In Node.js, what is the difference between `process.nextTick` and `setImmediate`, and in what order do they run relative to promise callbacks?
queries.gold_answer: nextTick runs before promise microtasks and before the event loop continues; setImmediate runs in the check phase of the next loop iteration

queries.text: How do I safely add a NOT NULL column with a default to a large Postgres table without a long exclusive lock, and which version made this cheap?
queries.gold_answer: Postgres 11 made adding a column with a non-volatile default a metadata-only operation, avoiding a full table rewrite

queries.text: In CSS, what is the difference between `contain: layout` and `content-visibility: auto`, and what rendering work does each skip?
queries.gold_answer: contain: layout isolates layout effects to the subtree; content-visibility: auto additionally skips rendering and layout of offscreen content entirely

queries.text: What is the difference between at-least-once and exactly-once delivery in Kafka, and what specifically must be configured for the latter?
queries.gold_answer: Exactly-once requires the idempotent producer plus transactions, with transactional.id set and consumers reading with read_committed isolation

queries.text: In Python, what does `functools.cache` do differently from `functools.lru_cache`, and what is the memory hazard of both on instance methods?
queries.gold_answer: cache is lru_cache with an unbounded maxsize; both keep references to self on methods, leaking instances for the process lifetime

queries.text: How does HTTP/2 head-of-line blocking differ from HTTP/1.1's, and what does HTTP/3 change about it?
queries.gold_answer: HTTP/2 removes application-level blocking but remains subject to TCP-level blocking; HTTP/3 over QUIC gives each stream its own loss recovery

queries.text: In Git, what is the difference between `--force` and `--force-with-lease` when pushing, and what race does the latter close?
queries.gold_answer: --force-with-lease refuses the push if the remote ref moved since you last fetched, preventing overwriting a colleague's commits

queries.text: What is a covering index, and how do I tell from an EXPLAIN plan in Postgres that one is being used?
queries.gold_answer: A covering index includes all columns the query needs, often via INCLUDE; the plan shows an Index Only Scan with low heap fetches

queries.text: In TypeScript, what is a discriminated union, and why does narrowing fail if the discriminant is not a literal type?
queries.gold_answer: A common literal-typed property lets the compiler narrow by comparison; a widened string type gives the compiler nothing to discriminate on

queries.text: How do I diagnose a memory leak in a long-running Python process, and which two standard-library tools are most directly useful?
queries.gold_answer: tracemalloc for allocation snapshots and gc for tracking uncollectable cycles and referrers

queries.text: In Terraform, what is the difference between `count` and `for_each`, and why does removing an element from a `count` list cause churn?
queries.gold_answer: count indexes resources positionally, so removing an element shifts indices and recreates resources; for_each keys them by a stable map key

queries.text: What does the `SameSite=Lax` cookie attribute actually block, and which common authentication flow does it break if set to Strict?
queries.gold_answer: Lax blocks cookies on cross-site subrequests but allows top-level GET navigation; Strict blocks the redirect back from an external identity provider

queries.text: In Java, what problem do virtual threads solve, in which release did they become a final feature, and what remains a pinning hazard?
queries.gold_answer: Virtual threads made cheap blocking concurrency practical, finalised in Java 21; synchronized blocks and native frames can pin a carrier thread

queries.text: How does a Bloom filter trade memory for accuracy, and what operation can it never support?
queries.gold_answer: It allows false positives but no false negatives, with error rate set by bits per element and hash count; standard Bloom filters cannot support deletion

queries.text: In Postgres, what is transaction ID wraparound, what happens if autovacuum cannot keep up, and which view shows how close you are?
queries.gold_answer: XIDs are 32-bit and wrap; the database refuses writes to protect data, and pg_database's datfrozenxid with age() shows the margin

queries.text: What is the difference between a hard link and a symbolic link on Linux, and which one breaks if the original file is renamed?
queries.gold_answer: A hard link references the inode and survives renaming; a symlink stores a path and breaks when the target is renamed or moved

queries.text: In npm, what is the difference between `npm ci` and `npm install`, and what does `npm ci` do if the lock file disagrees with package.json?
queries.gold_answer: npm ci installs strictly from the lock file into a clean node_modules and fails if the lock file and package.json are out of sync

queries.text: How do I implement exponential backoff with jitter correctly, and what specific failure does jitter prevent?
queries.gold_answer: Randomise the delay within the backoff window; without jitter, retrying clients synchronise into a thundering herd

queries.text: In Pandas 2.0, what changed about the default backend options, and what is the practical benefit of the Arrow-backed dtypes?
queries.gold_answer: Pandas 2.0 added optional PyArrow-backed dtypes, giving proper missing-value support across types and lower memory for strings

queries.text: What is the difference between OAuth 2.0's authorization code flow with PKCE and the implicit flow, and why was implicit deprecated?
queries.gold_answer: PKCE binds the code exchange to a client-generated verifier; implicit returned tokens in the URL fragment where they leak through history and referrers

queries.text: In Kubernetes, what is the difference between resource requests and limits for CPU, and what happens when a container exceeds each?
queries.gold_answer: Requests drive scheduling; exceeding a CPU limit throttles the container rather than killing it, unlike memory limits which trigger an OOM kill

queries.text: How do I make a Python package importable both as a script and as a module without the double-import problem, and what causes that problem?
queries.gold_answer: Use a __main__.py and run with -m; running a file directly puts its directory on sys.path and can import the same module under two names
